author: @apollo-2006

evidence.api_compatibility: The HTTP status code for 'repo has no supported files' and 'invalid manifest' cases changes from 500 to 400. This is a behavior change for clients that matched on 500, but 500 was incorrect (these are client errors, not server errors). The API docs in docs/api/lemonade.md were updated to reflect the new 400 rows and to remove those cases from the 500 description. This is a bug fix rather than a breaking change in the traditional sense, but existing clients that specifically caught 500 would need to handle 400 instead.
evidence.documentation: docs/api/lemonade.md updated: 400 row now covers 'repository has no GGUF, ONNX RyzenAI or collection files, its collection manifest is invalid or too large'; 500 row no longer lists those cases. The error message strings in src/cpp/server/routes/lemonade/models/pull_variants.cpp were updated to match.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The integration test is guarded by LEMONADE_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 and is skipped by default. There is no evidence that a human exercised the /pull/variants endpoint with a repository lacking supported files before merge. The change is user-visible (different HTTP status code on a real endpoint), so manual verification is needed before release.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after @fl0rianr's approval. The four commits (initial fix, oversized manifest fix, non-string recipe fix, log-level cleanup) were all approved as a unit.
evidence.review: PR #3673 received one substantive approval from @fl0rianr (LGTM) at 2026-11-18T11:10:18Z, right before merge. Per contribute.md, @fl0rianr's subject areas are LMX omni models, GUI, CI, and smart router — tangentially related via the omni collection manifest logic, but not deep expertise in the server error-handling path. No other human reviewer engaged. CodeRabbit bot raised one inline comment asking to add explicit "source": "huggingface" to the new integration test to avoid depending on default_model_source; the author addressed it. The change is small and self-contained, and the single review was adequate for the scope.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change replaces std::runtime_error with std::invalid_argument for invalid inputs, which is the correct C++ exception type for argument validation. No credential handling, network calls, or obfuscation changes.
evidence.tests: C++ unit tests added in test/cpp/test_hf_variants.cpp covering is_omni_collection_manifest: valid manifest accepted, non-string recipe rejected without throwing, non-collection recipe rejected, empty components rejected, empty object rejected, non-object rejected. Integration test added in test/server_endpoints.py (test_033_pull_variants_rejects_repo_without_supported_files) using Qwen/Qwen1.5-0.5B-Chat on Hugging Face, asserting 400 and the expected error message. All CI checks passed (Lemonade App checks, Server Download Registry Tests, C++ Server Build/Test/Release). No existing tests weakened or deleted.

maintainer_todos.text: Start lemond and request GET /pull/variants?checkpoint=Qwen/Qwen1.5-0.5B-Chat&source=huggingface and confirm the response is 400 with an error mentioning "No supported model files found" rather than 500.

subject: server: return 400 for repos with no supported model files (#3673)
summary: Changes the /pull/variants endpoint to return HTTP 400 (client error) instead of 500 (server error) when a Hugging Face or ModelScope repository contains no supported model files (no GGUF, ONNX, or collection manifest) or has an invalid or oversized collection manifest, and updates the API docs accordingly.
verdict_reason: The API behavior change is user-visible and the integration test that covers the end-to-end path is skipped by default, so no human has manually exercised the new 400 response before release.
